text:
incident-bot: Automated daily handoff summary for the 12h window ending 2025-06-01T20:00:00Z
- pagers: INC-7132 (resolved), INC-7139 (active, customer-facing tail errors), 7141 (info only)
- major alerts: high kv-cache memory growth on shard eu-west-1b
- impacted routes: /v1/generate (low qps customers), embeddings for customer corpX saw ~5% latency spikes

mike: Handoff — I'm primary for the shift. Quick state: INC-7132 was mitigated (hot loop in kv-cache GC patched, restarted pool). INC-7139 remains degraded: sporadic "kvcache OOM" on 3 nodes that host corpX and a small set of dev customers. We've pinned a temporary fallback to quantized model v2 on those hosts to keep responses stable.

sam: I'm secondary. Current coverage note: I'll be offline 14:00-16:00 UTC tomorrow for a scheduled doc review. Need someone to cover pages during that window; @jordan volunteered below but marking explicitly.

liz: Runbook pointers and quick commands: follow runbook sections "kv-cache/oom" -> https://runbooks.redwood.internal/kv-cache#oom
Helpful checks:
```
# List failing nodes (prod tag)
rgctl nodes list --tag prod --filter "kvcache.memory>80%"
# Grab heap summaries
ssh jump@eu-west-1b -- sudo /opt/redwood/bin/heap_snapshot --service kvcache --out /tmp/heap-$(date +%s).tgz
# Rollback step (if needed)
rgctl pool restart --group eu-west-1b-kvcache --graceful
```
Also, metric to watch: kvcache.heap_growth.rate (alert threshold 0.5 GB/min). If it sustains >0.5GB/min for 5m escalate to SRE pager.

ana: Customer impact summary for mobile and web features: corpX reported 4% request failures and some elevated tail latency for embeddings since 03:20 UTC. No data exfiltration or data loss. Affected customers are on dedicated pools; we have data isolation so blast radius limited. Ops note: CS notified corpX at 08:15 UTC and they're on a call with account.

jordan: I can pick up the 14:00-16:00 UTC coverage tomorrow. I'll be reachable via phone and Slack. If INC-7139 spikes, I'll coordinate with @mike for deeper trace and with @liz for runbook ops. :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks @jordan. Next actions (owner in parens):
- Stabilize remaining OOM nodes with graceful restarts + fallback routing (mike)
- Collect heap snapshots + determine leak vector (liz)
- Create a dedicated eval to reproduce growth under corpX workload (ana / research)
- Customer comms follow-up: update corpX with ETA and RC plan (cs-team / sam)

sam: I'll schedule the short escalation doc and leave clear notes in PagerDuty. Also adding an "on-call delegate" entry in the calendar to reflect @jordan covering that slot.

ana: For post-incident actions, suggest a small mitigation playbook: 1) detect: auto-snooze fallback when kvcache.memory>85% and 2) plan: schedule a small canary rollout of the GC patch on a single pool. I'll draft the eval and post to #eng-ml tomorrow.

mike: No immediate customer-wide impact beyond corpX's devs, but keep eyes open. If you see >2% failed requests across >3 customers, escalate to SEV-2 and notify @cto and incident channel.

incident-bot: Reminder: add the event to incident-tracker with tags [kv-cache, oom, corpX] and link traces: https://observability.redwood/traces?inc=7139

liz: One last ops tip — when doing graceful restarts, set env REDWOOD_KVCACHE_EVICT=1 for 60s to accelerate cold-warm warmup, avoids long tail spikes after restart.

mike: OK closing handoff. Primary: mike. Secondary: sam (but covered by jordan 14:00-16:00 UTC). Open items assigned above. Please ack in-thread so I can close the handoff ticket.

jordan: ack

sam: ack

liz: ack

mike: Thanks team :heart:
